overall: Atlanta is starting the day heavily overcast (OVC, 100% cloud cover, very low ceiling at ~183m) with temperatures locked in a remarkably tight range of 71–73°F overnight. A line of strong thunderstorms issued under Special Weather Statements from NWS Peachtree City was moving southeast away from the Atlanta area early this morning, leaving behind humid, cloud-covered conditions (dewpoint ~70°F) with essentially zero warming trend at the surface as of 06:34 ET.
forecast_obs_notes: The three NWP models are in unusually tight agreement: ECMWF=84.4°F, HRRR=84.8°F, NBM=83.9°F, all clustering 83.9–84.8°F versus the NWS official forecast of ~86°F. The intraday model predicts peak at ~14.1h (early-to-mid afternoon), while the NWP models push peak timing later to 16–17h — suggesting the models expect meaningful afternoon heating following a morning clearing, but the early storm activity and persistent OVC deck could compress the warming window and shave a degree or two off the peak.
max_temp_prediction: With models tightly packed around 84–85°F, the NWS calling for 86°F, and the bucket distribution peaking at 86–87°F (30%) but carrying meaningful weight in the 88–89°F bin (20%), the central estimate lands near 85–86°F. The main downside risks are the thick morning overcast delaying clearing and the 20% chance of afternoon convection (2–4 PM) prematurely capping warming; upside risk exists if the storm line clears quickly and allows several hours of strong June insolation. Confidence is moderate — model spread is tight but the morning cloud deck introduces meaningful intraday uncertainty.
